script: Am I the jerk for telling my mom I won't call her every day when I move out. I was 22, still living in my mom's house, trying to finish my degree. The apartment felt like a prison of her anxiety—every little thing was a potential crisis. I knew I had to leave, but my mom kept saying, "We're family, you can't just walk away." But here's the thing… My grandma lived across the world at 84, barely mobile, and she and my mom talked at least three times a day. Mom would freak out if grandma missed a call, blaming her for "forgetting" her phone in the yard. And when grandma mentioned the calls were too much, mom'd guilt‑trip her, saying she'd never call again. What I didn't know was that this was the family's entire rhythm—she lived and breathed her daughter's phone. The next day, we were talking about how often you should call parents. Mom said "at least once a day" and I said, "When I move out, there's no way I am calling you every single day." I wanted my own life, not a 24‑hour support crew. And that's when everything changed… Mom's face turned red. "If you do that, I am cutting off all financial support And that's the end of the story.
